You are a financial analysis assistant.  Below is background information taken from American Tower Corporation’s filings (table details are withheld):

American Tower Corporation selected December 1 as the date for annual impairment testing.  Internal appraisals performed for 2004-2005 concluded that goodwill in the rental & management segment was not impaired.  The company’s other intangible assets are amortised over periods ranging from three to fifteen years.  Amortisation of intangible assets (excluding deferred-financing-cost amortisation booked in interest expense) amounted to approximately $136.0 million in 2005 and $97.8 million in 2004.  Management expects to record amortisation expense of approximately $183.6 million, $178.3 million, $174.4 million, $172.7 million and $170.3 million for the fiscal years ending 2006-2010, respectively.  (All other details that appeared only in the numeric table have been omitted here.)

You can interact with the following tools to obtain data that are stored in an internal finance database.  All money values are USD unless noted.
• list_intangible_asset_categories() – returns every recorded intangible-asset category name.
• get_amortisable_intangible_categories() – returns the subset of categories that are amortisable.
• is_category_amortisable(category) – tells whether a single category is amortisable.
• get_accumulated_amortisation_thousand(category, year) – accumulated amortisation for a category at a given year-end (in thousands).
• get_annual_amortisation_expense(category, year) – amortisation expense for a category and year (in millions).
• convert_thousand_to_million(amount_thousand) – convert thousands → millions.
• sum_numbers(numbers) – sum a list of numeric amounts.
• goodwill_impairment_status() – returns goodwill impairment note.
• get_non_amortisable_categories() – returns categories that are not amortisable.

Think through what information you need, call the available tools as required, and respond with the single numeric answer (e.g., 123.4).  You may show reasoning, but the final answer must be on a line by itself so it can be automatically checked.
